questions.question: What makes a scientific hypothesis testable?
choices: Everyone agrees with it
Evidence could support or challenge it
It cannot be changed
It includes an exact date

questions.question: What is an observation?
choices: A conclusion that cannot be tested
A prediction about every future event
Information gathered using senses or instruments
An explanation based only on preference

questions.question: What is an inference?
choices: An explanation or conclusion drawn from observations
A procedure for measuring length
A direct instrument reading only
A result that requires no evidence

questions.question: What is a scientific theory?
choices: A personal opinion about nature
A claim that has not been investigated
A rule that never needs evidence
A broad explanation supported by substantial evidence

questions.question: What is a scientific model?
choices: A representation used to study or explain a system
A final answer that cannot be revised
A measurement with no uncertainty
An experiment without variables

questions.question: What does peer review involve?
choices: Students choosing the most popular conclusion
Replacing data with a scientist's reputation
Other qualified researchers evaluating scientific work
Publishing results without examining methods

questions.question: What does replication mean in scientific research?
choices: Changing every result to match an expectation
Using the same graph twice in a report
Removing results that differ from a prediction
Repeating a study or its methods to check findings

questions.question: Why should scientific explanations be open to revision?
choices: Earlier evidence has no value
New evidence may show that an explanation is incomplete
Scientists must change conclusions on a schedule
Every explanation is equally well supported

questions.question: How does an observational study differ from a controlled experiment?
choices: It cannot collect numerical data
It examines conditions without deliberately assigning a treatment
It never uses instruments
It must avoid forming any hypothesis

questions.question: Why does correlation alone not establish causation?
choices: Related variables can never affect each other
Causation is possible only in chemistry
A relationship becomes causal whenever a graph is drawn
Another factor or a different causal direction may explain the relationship

questions.question: How does a scientific law usually differ from a theory?
choices: A law describes a pattern, while a theory explains phenomena
A theory automatically becomes a law after enough time
A law is an unsupported guess and a theory is a measurement
Laws apply only to living organisms

questions.question: Why should researchers describe their methods clearly?
choices: It guarantees that every hypothesis is correct
It removes the need for recording data
It helps others evaluate and repeat the work
It makes conflicting evidence unnecessary

questions.question: What should researchers do when results contradict their hypothesis?
choices: Examine the methods and reconsider the hypothesis in light of the evidence
Discard all contradictory measurements automatically
Report only the measurements that fit
Treat the hypothesis as proven despite the results

questions.question: Why are several independent lines of evidence useful?
choices: They replace the need for reliable measurements
Agreement among different methods can strengthen confidence in an explanation
They guarantee there is no uncertainty
They make peer review unnecessary

questions.question: Why must scientists distinguish evidence from interpretation?
choices: Interpretations can never be useful
Evidence always explains itself completely
Readers need to see what was observed and how conclusions were drawn
Only interpretations belong in reports

questions.question: A student notices leaves bending toward a window and proposes that light affects growth direction. Which statement is a testable explanatory hypothesis?
choices: The leaves were observed near a window
The window faces east
The plant has six leaves
Light affects the direction of plant growth

questions.question: More ice cream is sold on days with more swimming accidents. Which explanation should be considered before claiming a direct cause?
choices: The two measurements must be fabricated
Ice cream sales prove that food causes every accident
Hot weather may increase both swimming and ice cream sales
Correlation makes other explanations impossible

questions.question: Two studies reach different conclusions. What is the best next scientific step?
choices: Compare their methods, data, and limitations
Accept whichever was published first
Choose the conclusion with the most memorable title
Ignore both without examining their evidence

questions.question: A model predicts a river will flood, but it excludes a newly built levee. What should researchers examine?
choices: Whether models can ever use numbers
Whether the river has a name
Whether the prediction agrees with public opinion
How the missing feature affects the model's assumptions and prediction

questions.question: Which conclusion best matches a single successful experiment?
choices: The explanation is permanently proven for every situation
The findings support the hypothesis under the tested conditions
All alternative explanations have been eliminated
No further investigation is useful
